chapter: The Los Angeles music scene in the early 1930s
title: Lionel Hampton's company, Leon Herriford and Baby Lewis
summary: Blakeney recalls musicians such as Leon Herriford criticizing Hampton for the company he kept, the fraternal feeling among musicians, and drummer Baby Lewis.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: We've spoken as to how the community felt about some of the musicians; what was the attitude of some musicians towards their peers, the stronger, more proficient players; how did some of the less skilled musicians look at them, and vice-versa?
Well, you take guys like Lionel, he was considered a rabble rouser. You'd see him around with some of
the lesser known musicians. He wasn't particular about who he ran with.
I can remember the time he was criticized for being out with a bunch he shouldn't have been.
This is what I had reference to, this kind of respect or disrespect; whatever you call it.
Were there the usual petty jealousies among the musicians?
Yes, there were in a way.
Leon used to critize Lionel about how he used to run around, the type of fellows he used to run around with, he shouldn't do it.
Was the name Leon?
Leon Heriford.
What did he play, Mr. Blakeney?
Saxophone. He was a fine musician, one of the finest during
that time, as a saxophone man. He had a pretty tone.
Did he ever speak to Lionel about it?
Oh yes, yes.
And what was his response if you can recall?
His response was it's not their concern who he runs around with on his days off.
It's his own business?
That's right.

Was there more of a fraternal feeling among the musicians, the welfare of their fellow musicians? Were physically they concerned about each other, about how they were getting along, if they had a job, about their circumstances at home? Was there a feeling of fraternity?
There was a feeling of fraternity among some of the musicians towards others. Sometimes Lionel would be

in the center of it because he was running around with different guys that he shouln't have, we thought because he was too decent to be running around with certain kinds of musicians. I thought that Lionel had a problem.
Was Mr. Hampton married to Gladys Hampton at this time?
I don't think he was married to her; no.
He was perhaps about one of the youngest in the group about that time; is that right?
That's right; yes. Him and Baby Lewis were about the same age, I guess.
Is that Baby Lewis?
Yes.
What did Baby Lewis play?
Drums, like Lionel.
Were they friends?
Oh, yes, with each other. Both of them were kind of eccentric on the drums; they played vibes.
Both of them were eccentric on the drums?
Yes. Also Baby Lewis was better than Lionel.
Baby Lewis was a contemporary of Lionel?
Yes; right.
